scope: Prerequisite source assessment for a private Codex request hook and access-token workspace parser. No product implementation, package execution, tests, validator, platform acceptance, or full dependency closure.
reasoning_effort: xhigh, inherited/configured for credential and cancellation boundaries

conclusion.request_hook: The locked native reqwest API supports the proposed boundary without a new client, custom transport, or dependency patch. Build the real request, inspect it privately, and execute it with its embedded client. Preserve builder errors inside the future observed by await_reqwest so cancellation remains dominant.
conclusion.observation_limit: The hook observes the final application-created URL, auth/account headers and serialized body. It precedes client-default, proxy and lower HTTP-layer additions; it is not an observation of every final wire header or of real ChatGPT service acceptance.
conclusion.jwt_decoder: The existing URL_SAFE_NO_PAD engine is suitable for strict unpadded base64url payload decoding. It rejects padding, nonalphabet/whitespace input and nonzero discarded trailing bits. Exact JWT component count, JSON object/claim typing and workspace equality remain caller responsibilities.
conclusion.dependency_changes: No version, feature, source patch, vendoring or added dependency is needed for these mechanics.
conclusion.acceptance: Source-supported mechanics only. Root retains the resume-compatibility decision and implementation ownership.

request_contract.fact: RequestBuilder stores its original Client plus Result<Request>. header() appends a converted header, stores conversion errors in that Result, and does not dispatch. json(), gated by feature json, serializes once with serde_json::to_vec, preserves an explicitly supplied Content-Type and stores a reusable byte body. Serialization errors are retained as reqwest builder errors.
request_contract.implication: Place the hook after these actual calls. Assert one expected Authorization and one account header; do not replace the credential loader or reproduce serialization in the fixture.

request_contract.fact: build() returns the stored Result<Request>; build_split() returns that result and its original Client. send() dispatches valid requests to Client::execute_request or wraps the exact stored error in Pending::new_err. Public Client::execute calls the same execute_request. Client clones retain the same Arc<ClientRef>.
request_contract.implication: Prefer build_split to avoid accidentally selecting another client. Keep the complete Request and its method, version, timeout extensions, body and headers; change only the destination URL under an armed cfg(test) scope.

request_contract.fact: The Host cancellation wrapper checks should_cancel before polling the reqwest future and maps its reqwest error to ProviderSessionError::Transport only after the cancellable await. A stored builder error in send() is therefore still subject to that cancellation check.
request_contract.required_shape: Pass a future equivalent to: async move { let (client, built) = builder.build_split(); let mut request = built?; invoke_private_test_hook_if_armed(&mut request); client.execute(request).await } into the existing await_reqwest with the same cancellation callback and label. The hook is cfg(test) only.
request_contract.refusal: Do not use an eager build()? or convert the builder error to Authentication/Protocol before entering await_reqwest. Do not spawn a detached send, create a replacement cancellation loop, or bypass the existing polling/typed error path.
request_contract.timing_limit: Constructing/serializing the builder still occurs at the existing site. In the proposed future, execute and hook entry begin after the first cancellation check; no exact scheduling or wire-send timing equivalence is claimed.

request_contract.fact: Request exposes url/url_mut, headers/headers_mut and body/body_mut. A JSON Vec<u8> or the existing OAuth form String creates a reusable Body; as_bytes returns its existing bytes without consuming it. A streaming Body returns None.
request_contract.implication: Inspect method, original URL, headers and body().and_then(Body::as_bytes), then mutate only url_mut for loopback. Do not remove/rebuild the body or reconstruct headers. A fixture expecting JSON/form bytes must fail if it sees a streaming/absent body.

request_contract.fact: execute_request validates scheme/https_only, fills only vacant header names from client defaults, applies proxy handling, creates the underlying request and establishes client/request timeout state. Existing request headers win over client defaults. HTTP proxy custom headers can be inserted later.
request_contract.implication: Use the original client and execute path to preserve defaults, connection pool and timeout behavior. Do not describe the pre-execute hook as seeing final Host/Content-Length/proxy headers. The present Host shared client configures pool/keepalive and no default auth header.

request_contract.fact: ClientBuilder starts with Accept */*, auto system proxy enabled and normal redirect/retry policy. Build installs the system matcher when enabled. reqwest's NoProxy contract documents NO_PROXY/no_proxy and '*' matching all hostnames; system matching delegates to hyper-util.
request_contract.fixture_requirement: The owned child must establish proxy-isolated synthetic environment before initializing the shared client: remove inherited HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY and lowercase variants, set owned NO_PROXY/no_proxy for all destinations, and use a fixture-owned literal loopback address. Observe the loopback server's actual receipt and return no redirects. Do not change production proxy/client policy to make the test pass.
request_contract.limit: Hyper-util's proxy resolver, OS proxy implementation and redirect/retry internals were not fully read; this report does not certify general network isolation or all transport behavior.

private_scope_contract.location: Below read_codex_credentials and actual final request header/body construction, immediately before execute. Distinguish Codex inference and Codex OAuth refresh requests privately; do not intercept the unrelated Native branch merely because it shares send_codex_request.
private_scope_contract.precedent: The existing CMI RefCell<Option<Rc<...>>> scope releases its borrow before calling user callbacks, retains the previous scope, checks owner ThreadId and is !Send through PhantomData<Rc<()>> (codex_model_identity_tests.rs:84-117). Reuse that custody pattern, not its mock-transport boundary.
requirements: Registration remains private under cfg(test), with no production env/config/public endpoint override. Production credentials and fixed URLs are still constructed by the same owner.

Release the thread-local borrow before invoking the callback. Capture/validate an owner-thread scope token; do not silently fall through to a real endpoint if execution moves away from the armed scope.
Run the hook synchronously before the network await; hold no RefCell borrow across an await, do not move its Rc/guard into tokio::spawn, and do not create an extra executor.

Assert the original fixed production URL, POST method, expected one-account/one-bearer header pair and actual body first. Redirect only that recognized synthetic request to the owned fixture. Unexpected request kinds/destinations fail closed in the armed fixture.

Retain bounded child/server retirement and restore scope on Drop. No callback or captured request may outlive its scope. Never Debug-print a real Request: header() uses sensitive=false unless the supplied value was already marked sensitive.
The server observes actual loopback requests; this establishes the local credential/header/Runner behavior only, not TLS or real provider acceptance.
necessary_actions_oracles_not_run: Cancellation already true plus a builder error: Cancelled, zero hook entries and zero sends.
Builder error without cancellation: existing Transport result, zero hook entries and zero sends; no swallowed or reclassified reqwest error.
Valid built request: hook observes the original fixed URL/auth/account/body, then loopback receipt confirms those application headers/body were retained.
Existing account-switch, same-account rotation, checkpoint/custody and refresh-response cases use this boundary, not the earlier CMI TransportFactory that skips credential reading.

base64_contract.fact: URL_SAFE_NO_PAD is GeneralPurpose(URL_SAFE, NO_PAD). URL_SAFE uses A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-' and '_'. The decode table marks every other byte invalid; '+' and '/', whitespace and non-ASCII bytes are not alternative accepted alphabet characters.

NO_PAD changes the default config to encode_padding=false and DecodePaddingMode::RequireNone. decode_allow_trailing_bits remains false. The actual suffix decoder rejects any suffix padding, illegal/interior padding, invalid final symbol count and nonzero discarded bits.
base64_contract.consequences: Do not add padding, strip '=', trim payload whitespace, swap alphabets, set DecodePaddingMode::Indifferent, or enable trailing-bit forgiveness. A payload whose encoded length is 1 modulo 4 is invalid. Valid unpadded lengths modulo 4 are 0, 2 or 3, subject to the final-bit rules.
base64_contract.error_limit: Do not assert one specific DecodeError variant for every malformed input: invalid padding can be classified as InvalidByte before the final InvalidPadding check.

base64_contract.fact: Engine::decode is enabled by alloc, allocates a conservatively sized Vec, invokes the selected engine's internal decoder, returns DecodeError on failure and truncates the successful output. Default std enables alloc in this package.
base64_contract.implication: Use the existing imported Engine/URL_SAFE_NO_PAD directly; no new decoder package or custom decoder is required. This decoder does not validate JWT structure or signatures.

base64_contract.required_parser_boundary: Count exactly three '.'-separated components, rejecting a missing third or any fourth component rather than split('.').nth(1) alone. Decode only the payload with URL_SAFE_NO_PAD, parse the decoded bytes as a JSON object, require the named auth claim to be an object and its workspace to be a nonempty string, then apply the established exact file/account/binding comparison.
base64_contract.caller_limit: The base64 dependency neither checks header/signature components nor requires them to be nonempty. Any stronger header/signature shape rule is an explicit product contract choice; metadata parsing is not signature, issuer, expiry or principal verification.
base64_contract.compatibility_limit: This report establishes strict Rust decoder behavior. It does not claim identical acceptance of malformed base64 to fixed-U's Node Buffer decoder. Ordinary unpadded URL-safe JWT payloads are the intended shape.
base64_contract.errors: Map failure to the scoped generic credential Authentication refusal. Do not include the token, decoded JSON or raw credential document in diagnostics.
